excerpt: Veriff is an Estonian identity verification company. What it does, its published per-verification pricing, funding history and alternatives.
content:
Veriff is an identity verification company founded in Estonia in 2015. Businesses use it to check that a new user is a real person holding a genuine ID document, typically when opening an account, to meet know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering rules or to stop fraud. The user takes a photo of their ID and a selfie or short video, and Veriff's system decides whether to approve, decline or send the case for review. TechCrunch described its distinguishing feature as AI-powered video verification, and SecurityWeek reported that it checks more than 1,000 data points.

Veriff raised a $69 million Series B in April 2021. In January 2022 it raised a $100 million Series C co-led by Tiger Global and Alkeon, with existing investors IVP and Accel, which TechCrunch reported valued it at $1.5 billion and brought total funding to $200 million. At the time it had offices in the US, UK, Spain and Estonia and more than 360 employees.

Unlike many verification vendors, Veriff publishes self-serve prices. Its pricing page lists three plans charged per verification with a monthly minimum: Essential (fully automated AI checks) at $0.80 per verification with a $49 monthly minimum, Plus (AI plus human verification specialists) at $1.39 with a $99 minimum, and Premium at $1.89 with a $209 minimum. Enterprise pricing is negotiated and aimed at more than 5,000 verifications a month. Add-ons include PEP and sanctions screening and ongoing monitoring, and a free trial covers up to 50 sessions.

Veriff suits fintechs, marketplaces, gaming, mobility and other companies that must verify users remotely. Very small projects may find the monthly minimum more than they need.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
